Beside the options the agent takes two mode words. `statusline-echo`, landed at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through: it prints its output and files its stdin, and its exit is the code after the marker path.
 `agents` (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board): a first word `agents` answers `agents --json` from files beside its exe (`agents-mode`, `agents-rows.json`, and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry: a row written just before its launch SessionStart fires, its `cwd` the launch fixture's recorded `cwd`, `~` without one; a dead or reused pid skipped through one `viola_state::liveness::start_times()` read), built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`; no option and no env are added; units `agents_output_*`, `live_sessions_skip_a_dead_or_reused_pid`, `launch_session_replays_the_recorded_id_and_cwd` and `planted_rows_of_a_malformed_rows_file_are_none`. Every workflow (`ci.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `windows-mutants.yml`) has `permissions: {}` at the top and `contents: read` per job. Every `uses:` is SHA-pinned; zizmor `unpinned-uses` is the assertion. Tools are installed with taiki-e/install-action v2.87.19 (SHA-pinned) as `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1,cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-deny@0.20.2`; `windows-mutants.yml` installs `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-mutants@27.1.0` with the same action, and `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` asserts those two pins equal the `test` job's `tool:` line. hyperfine 1.20.0, cargo-modules 0.27.0 and zizmor 1.30.1 are installed with `cargo install --locked <crate>@<version>` in the jobs that invoke them. G2 (`scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh`, in the `test` and `perf` jobs), `scripts/orphans-check.sh` (`lint`) and `scripts/release-check.sh` (`release`) use the runner-provided `jq`, never installed: the `test` and `perf` jobs presence-check it (`jq --version`) and all three scripts refuse with `tool-missing: jq`. ripgrep 15.2.0, the G1/G3 tool, comes from `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh` (pinned, checksum-verified official release) in the `lint` job. cargo-fuzz 0.13.2 is installed with `cargo install --locked`, only in the `fuzz-replay` and nightly `fuzz` jobs, with the channel from `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml`. See §3 Bootstrap `ci-tool-install`. rustfmt and clippy come from `rust-toolchain.toml` `components`, installed by the `rustup toolchain install` step (no toolchain action; the MSRV and fuzz jobs, which need a different toolchain, name theirs). cargo-deny and zizmor run as the pinned CLIs above; cargo-deny-action and zizmor-action are not used, so each tool has exactly one version source.
 The local pre-push gate runs natively on the Linux dev host and installs nothing: its `tools` stage checks the host's `cc`, the `rust-toolchain.toml` channel, the pins it parses from the `test` job's `tool:` line (cargo-nextest 0.9.146, cargo-mutants 27.1.0, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, as read on the Linux dev host 2026-10-04), refusing a missing or off-pin tool with `tool-missing` / `tool-pin-mismatch` — so ci.yml stays the one version source. No provisioning script remains. cargo-deny 0.20 takes `--config <path>` as a global option before the subcommand; `check -c` is rejected (as measured on cargo-deny 0.20.2, dev host, 2026-09-24).
No workflow (`ci.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `windows-mutants.yml`) has a `concurrency:` block: a concurrency group cancels pending runs even with `cancel-in-progress: false`, which would drop a push's `always()` gate and upload chain. zizmor's pedantic `concurrency-limits` finding is declined and stays visible (3 low, one per workflow; zizmor 1.30.1 on the dev host, 2026-10-04).
